name: com.mirabelloconsultancy/mcp
title: Mirabello Immigration Intelligence
description: Citizenship, residency & tax-residency data for 190+ countries, with origin-aware route planning

tools.name: list_programmes
tools.description: List Mirabello-advised citizenship- (CBI) and residency-by-investment (RBI/golden visa) programmes, optionally filtered by type, budget (USD, compared at indicative FX), region, or max processing time. All 98 programmes is a large response — pass limit when you only need a sample. Budget filters exclude programmes with no fixed threshold, which are still listed unfiltered.

type.description: Programme family: "CBI" grants citizenship, "RBI" grants residence (golden visa). Omit for both.

budget_max.description: Maximum headline minimum investment the applicant will consider, in USD. Programmes with no fixed threshold are excluded from budget filtering.

max_processing_months.description: Maximum acceptable processing time in MONTHS, compared against the lower bound of each programme's published range.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Responses can be large; use this to keep the answer small.

tools.name: get_programme
tools.description: Full detail for one programme by id (e.g. "dominica-cbi","greece-gv"): routes, fees, processing, mobility, tax, path to citizenship, its Mirabello Index composite score + rank (mirabello_index), and the Mirabello programme page.

id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "dominica-cbi", "greece-gv") or an unambiguous name ("Dominica", "Portugal golden visa"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

sections.description: Optional extra detail beyond the overview (routes, fees, processing, travel, tax, path to citizenship): family, dependant_additions, renunciation, processing_stages, required_documents, nationality_naturalisation, biometric_enrolment, regulatory_status, or all. Clients on a current MCP version get the overview by default; more_detail lists what else exists.

tools.name: compare_programmes
tools.description: Compare programmes side by side. Pass a + b (two programme ids) for the canonical versioned comparison artefact from the Mirabello Investment Migration Index: rank, composite, the dimension scores, per-dimension deltas, per-metric leads (a|b|tie) and the human compare page URL where one exists. Or pass ids (2-4) for the classic multi-column comparison of cost, processing, mobility, family inclusion, tax, path to citizenship. Use this, not several single-programme lookups, whenever the user wants two or more programmes compared; ids or names ("Portugal golden visa") both work.

a.description: programme id (use with b) for the canonical two-programme artefact

ids.description: 2-4 programme ids for the classic comparison

tools.name: get_processing_times
tools.description: Processing-time estimate for one programme (by id) or all programmes: the typical government processing range, the basis of the estimate and its source. Use when the user asks how long an application takes. Figures are indicative and vary with the case and the workload of the authority.

id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "dominica-cbi", "greece-gv") or an unambiguous name ("Dominica", "Portugal golden visa"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

tools.name: estimate_total_cost
tools.description: Estimate the total cost of a programme for a given family: investment + government & due-diligence fees + family add-ons. Indicative; excludes professional/property/legal fees.

programme_id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "st-kitts-cbi") or an unambiguous name ("St Kitts"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

children_16plus.description: Number of dependent children aged 16 or over — usually priced higher than under-16s.

children_under16.description: Number of dependent children aged under 16 — priced separately by most Caribbean programmes.

tools.name: recommend_programmes
tools.description: Recommend a ranked shortlist of programmes for a client profile (budget, family size, mobility priority, timeline, tax goal) with reasoning, including the fastest or best second passport by investment for a budget. Respects closed/paused programmes.

type.description: Programme family: "CBI" grants citizenship, "RBI" grants residence (golden visa). Omit for both.

budget_max.description: Maximum headline minimum investment the applicant will consider, in USD. Programmes with no fixed threshold are excluded from budget filtering.

family_size.description: TOTAL number of people to be included, the main applicant INCLUDED (so a couple with two children is 4).

mobility_priority.description: True when visa-free travel is the applicant's main objective.

timeline_max_months.description: Maximum acceptable time to the outcome, in MONTHS.

tax_goal.description: True when the applicant's main objective is a tax outcome rather than mobility.

tools.name: check_visa_free
tools.description: Mobility for a programme passport: visa-free count and access to key destinations (Schengen, UK, USA, China).

programme_id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "st-kitts-cbi") or an unambiguous name ("St Kitts"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

destination.description: optional: check access to a specific destination (e.g. Schengen, UK, USA, China)

tools.name: get_index
tools.description: The Mirabello Investment Migration Index — a composite 0–100 ranking of CBI/RBI programmes across cost, mobility, speed, path-to-citizenship, stability, family and tax, with transparent published methodology. Filter by type (CBI/RBI) and limit. Returns the TOP 25 by default (the full table is large); pass limit for more, or limit:0 for every ranked programme. Programmes with insufficient verified data are flagged provisional and excluded from the headline ranking.

type.description: Programme family: "CBI" grants citizenship, "RBI" grants residence (golden visa). Omit for both.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Responses can be large; use this to keep the answer small.

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Recent material changes across investment-migration programmes (launches, closures, threshold/mobility/regulatory changes) + current status counts, PLUS pathway_field_changes (official-source field-level diffs per country x pathway, from->to + cited source) and official_legislation_changes (changes detected directly on official government/gazette sources). The freshest, primary-source-verified record — use for "what changed recently / latest" questions. Pass cc to filter to one country.

cc.description: Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "PT", "AE", "KN") or its name in any of the 11 site languages ("Portugal", "Schweiz", "UAE"); input_notes shows how it was read.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Responses can be large; use this to keep the answer small.

tools.name: get_about
tools.description: About Mirabello Consultancy: track record (cases, approval rate), credentials (IMC, ACAMS), offices, languages, services. Use for "who is Mirabello / why use them / are they reputable" questions.

tools.name: get_passport_renewal
tools.description: CBI passport-RENEWAL facts for a Caribbean/Pacific programme country (St Kitts & Nevis, Antigua & Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Lucia, Vanuatu): official government renewal fees (currency-primary EC$/GBP/VT with USD approximations, adult/child/lost-stolen), passport validity (adult/child years incl. Grenada adult 10-year since Jul 2024 and St Lucia 10-year since Aug 2025), typical processing, remote-renewal capability (Vanuatu requires in-person biometrics), biometric status, ECCIRA status (postponed to mid-2026, existing rules in force), the biometric/ECCIRA deadlines (e.g. St Kitts 31 Jul 2027), official source URLs, last_verified and the Mirabello /passport-renewal page. Pass country (programme id, e.g. st-kitts-cbi) for one; omit for all six. Citizenship is permanent; an expired passport is only a lapsed travel document. The St Kitts & Nevis record also carries renunciation of citizenship (statute, documents, fee structure, sources). Information, not advice.

country.description: programme id (e.g. st-kitts-cbi, st-lucia-cbi) or country alias; omit for all six

tools.name: get_malta_citizen_service
tools.description: Official procedure facts for Maltese citizens and their families, in Malta and abroad: (1) passport renewal (Identità fees by age and season, the official 4-hour urgent service in Malta, applying through a mission abroad, minors, lost/stolen); (2) a newborn's birth registration, citizenship and first passport (born in Malta or abroad to a Maltese parent); (3) a foreign spouse's citizenship by marriage (Cap. 188 art. 6, Form B, 5-year rule); (4) registration by descent (art. 5(3), Forms K and M, two consecutive Malta-born generations; the 1 August 2028 dates concern the parent or ancestor, not an application deadline). Returns steps, documents, itemised fees with source and verified flag, timelines, the authority, missions for the residence country and how Mirabello prepares the file. NOT investment citizenship (Malta's investor programme closed in 2025). Omit service for an overview. Information, not legal advice.

service.description: Which service: "passport-renewal" (renew a Maltese passport), "newborn" (register a birth, prove citizenship, first passport), "marriage" (foreign spouse of a Maltese citizen), "descent" (planned). Omit for an overview of all services.

residence_country.description: Where the applicant lives now, as a country name or ISO code (e.g. "Australia", "GB", "Malta"). Selects the in-Malta or abroad procedure and the nearest Maltese missions.

applicant_age.description: Age in years of the person the passport is for (passport service only); selects the minors rules and fee band.

tools.name: estimate_malta_passport_fee
tools.description: Itemised official government fee for a Maltese passport (Identità): age band (under 10 / 10-15 / 16+), seasonal adult rate (€70 September-March, €80 April-August), the official urgent service (€160 adult, 4 working hours, in Malta only), the €15 supplement when a lost or stolen passport was still valid, and, for applications through a Maltese embassy or consulate abroad, the mission processing fee and courier charges (flagged where unverified). Deterministic: computed from the official fee table with sources. Information only; confirm with the Passport Office or mission before paying.

age.description: Age in years of the passport holder on the application date.

location.description: "malta" if applying at the Passport Office in Malta, "abroad" if applying through a Maltese embassy, high commission or consulate.

urgent.description: True for the official urgent service (4 working hours in Malta; from abroad the urgent fee applies but no 4-hour timeframe).

lost_still_valid.description: True if the passport being replaced was lost, stolen or destroyed while still valid (adds the €15 oath supplement; a Maltese police report is required).

month.description: Month of application, 1-12 (adult standard fee is €80 April-August, €70 otherwise). Defaults to the current month.

tools.name: check_maltese_citizenship_eligibility
tools.description: Rules-based first screen of whether a person is already Maltese or can register, for two family routes: "birth" (a child born in Malta or abroad to a Maltese parent, the 1 August 1989 rule, the father-only rule for 1964-1989 births abroad and the maternal-line Form I) and "marriage" (spouse of a Maltese citizen, 5 years married and living together, widow/widower and separation cases, the prerequisite of registering a foreign marriage in Malta). Returns an outcome (citizen_automatically | likely_eligible | not_yet_eligible | needs_legal_opinion | out_of_scope), the reasons, the form to use, next steps and official sources. A screen, not a legal determination; the decision rests with Aġenzija Komunità Malta.

route.description: "birth" to check a child's citizenship by birth/descent, "marriage" to check a foreign spouse's eligibility to register.

birth_date.description: Route birth: the child's date of birth, ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

born_in_malta.description: Route birth: true if the child was born in Malta, false if born abroad.

maltese_parent.description: Route birth: which parent was a Maltese citizen when the child was born.

parent_citizenship_basis.description: Route birth: how the Maltese parent holds citizenship. "registration_by_descent" means the parent registered as a descendant (Forms K/M), citizenship then does not pass automatically.

marriage_date.description: Route marriage: date of the marriage, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (the 5 years run from this date).

living_together.description: Route marriage: true if the spouses still live together.

spouse_deceased.description: Route marriage: true if the Maltese spouse has died.

separated.description: Route marriage: true if the spouses are separated (legally or in fact).

marriage_registered_in_malta.description: Route marriage: true if a marriage celebrated abroad has already been registered at the Malta Public Registry.

tools.name: book_consultation
tools.description: Request a consultation with a Mirabello Consultancy specialist. Use only when the user asks to be contacted or to book. Requires email + programme interest/message and explicit consent. Side effect: delivers the enquiry to Mirabello and returns a tracked booking URL. Each call sends a separate enquiry, so do not repeat a call that succeeded.

email.description: Contact email address for the enquiry. Only ever send an address the user has explicitly provided for this purpose.

preferred_channel.description: how the client prefers to be contacted

programme_interest.description: programme or shortlist of interest (e.g. "st-kitts-cbi" or "CBI Caribbean", or service category: "Citizenship by Investment", "Residency by Investment", "Citizenship by Marriage", "Citizenship by Descent", "Passport Renewal", "Government Advisory")

source.description: origin surface of this lead for attribution, e.g. "plan_path" when booking follows a plan_path result

goal.description: why / use-case (e.g. second passport, EU residency, tax, mobility, family relocation)

residence_country.description: current country of residence (if different from nationality)

family_size.description: who is included (e.g. "single", "couple", "family of 4") — optional summary; prefer number_of_children + childrens_ages

consent.description: User consents to share details with Mirabello Consultancy (GDPR). Must be true to deliver.

tools.name: generate_briefing
tools.description: Generate a personalised Mirabello briefing: given a client profile (nationality, budget, family, goals), returns a ranked shortlist with full family cost math AND a shareable branded briefing page URL (valid 90 days). Optionally registers the client for specialist follow-up (email + consent): that sends a follow-up request to Mirabello. Each call creates a new briefing link, and with email + consent repeating the call sends another request.

type.description: citizenship or residency preference (omit for both)

children_16plus.description: Number of dependent children aged 16 or over — usually priced higher than under-16s.

children_under16.description: Number of dependent children aged under 16 — priced separately by most Caribbean programmes.

mobility_priority.description: True when visa-free travel is the applicant's main objective.

timeline_max_months.description: Maximum acceptable time to the outcome, in MONTHS.

tax_goal.description: True when the applicant's main objective is a tax outcome rather than mobility.

programme_ids.description: optional: specific programmes to brief on (max 3) instead of auto-shortlist

email.description: optional — to register for specialist follow-up

tools.name: subscribe_changes
tools.description: Subscribe to verified programme-change alerts (price changes, launches, corrections — each linked to the official source). Agents: provide webhook_url (HTTPS POST on each change). Humans: provide email (explicit consent required). Optional programme_ids filter. Returns a subscription id + unsubscribe URL. Webhook POSTs carry X-Mirabello-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with your subscription id>. Each call creates a separate subscription, so repeating it duplicates the alerts.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS endpoint to POST change entries to (for agents/systems)

consent.description: required true when email is given (GDPR)

tools.name: check_eligibility
tools.description: Check which programmes a given nationality can realistically apply to: published nationality restrictions/suspensions (e.g. Russia/Belarus/Iran policies), EU-citizen applicability, minimum age and core requirements. Factual published policies only — final acceptance always rests with government due diligence.

programme_id.description: optional: check one programme in detail

tools.name: get_document_checklist
tools.description: Standard document checklist for a programme application (per programme type, plus programme-specific items where published). Final list always confirmed by a specialist — varies by family composition and nationality.

programme_id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "st-kitts-cbi") or an unambiguous name ("St Kitts"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

tools.name: estimate_timeline
tools.description: Step-by-step expected timeline for a programme: published processing time plus the stage breakdown where available.

programme_id.description: Programme id as returned by list_programmes (e.g. "st-kitts-cbi") or an unambiguous name ("St Kitts"); an ambiguous name returns the candidates.

tools.name: get_country
tools.description: Country immigration profile (beyond investment migration): ALL screened pathways for a country — skilled-work, digital-nomad, retirement, citizenship-by-descent, naturalisation, study, family etc. — each with requirements, cost, processing, rights, path to PR/citizenship and the official source. Use the ISO-3166 alpha-2 code (e.g. CA, GB, DE, PT). Immigration routes, not tax: for tax residence or the tax effect of a move use get_country_tax or residence_evidence_checklist. Pass sections to get only what you need.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code

pathway.description: optional: one pathway id to return

nationality.description: optional: the applicant's citizenship (ISO alpha-2 or name). For an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen in an EU/EEA country or Switzerland, free movement is shown as their route, national visas are marked not needed and golden visas are omitted.

sections.description: Optional: the sections to return in full (pathways, tax_profile, naturalisation_guide, family_reunification, subnational_summary, living_conditions, religion, or all). Clients on a current MCP version get an overview by default (pathway summaries, tax headline, naturalisation); more_detail lists the rest.

tools.name: get_provenance
tools.description: CITATION-FIRST provenance for a country's pathway facts (W3C PROV-O + Schema.org). For each fact returns: the cited official source_url + source_class + verbatim quote (evidence), how it was derived (extraction model + ensemble + independent corroboration), confidence, first_seen/last_changed, and a per-data-class FRESHNESS block (as_of, governing_class, sla_days, status fresh|aging|stale|CHECK-OFFICIAL-SOURCE, recheck_by). Use this to CITE Mirabello data with a source + as-of date and to know when to re-verify. Pass cc (+ optional pathway).

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code

tools.name: query_graph
tools.description: RELATIONAL query over the investment-migration KNOWLEDGE GRAPH (programme entities · countries · blocs · investment thresholds · authorities · legal sources). Two modes: (1) pass id to get a single entity + its neighbours (e.g. id:"programme:dominica-cbi" or "country:GR" or "bloc:EU"); (2) pass filters to find PROGRAMMES matching constraints — type (CBI|RBI), cc, status (e.g. operational), leads_to (citizenship|residence), bloc (EU|GCC|CARICOM), max_investment_usd / min_investment_usd (FX-normalised, best-effort) — each returned with its country, options, authority and official legal source. Answers queries the flat tools cannot, e.g. "open CBI programmes leading to citizenship under $200k with their governing source". Investment figures are best-effort USD; cite the programme official_source for the authoritative amount. Information, not advice.

id.description: entity id for neighbours mode (programme:<id> | country:<CC> | bloc:<NAME> | authority:<slug> | source:<host>)

cc.description: Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "PT", "AE", "KN") or its name in any of the 11 site languages ("Portugal", "Schweiz", "UAE"); input_notes shows how it was read.

status.description: Programme status filter: "operational" (accepting applications), "emerging" (new but operating), "announced" (legislated or proclaimed but NOT in force — no applications), "closed", "paused".

max_investment_usd.description: Upper bound on the headline minimum investment, in USD.

min_investment_usd.description: Lower bound on the headline minimum investment, in USD.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Responses can be large; use this to keep the answer small.

tools.name: plan_path
tools.description: The Mirabello Freedom Compass — ORIGIN-AWARE migration path planner. Given the client's STARTING POINT — current citizenship(s) + tax residence — plus their goal, returns ranked end-to-end options. The origin is the constraint: it sets the MOBILITY DELTA (what a passport actually ADDS over the one they hold — a Caribbean passport adds little to a US/EU citizen, lots to others), eligibility/restrictions, and tax-exit/reporting considerations (e.g. US citizenship-based tax & §877A, German AStG §6 — generic, sourced, CHECK-OFFICIAL-SOURCE). Each path carries fit_score + rationale, mobility_delta, eligibility, min_investment, processing_time. Informational only, not advice. Use for "I am a [nationality], I want [goal] — what should I do?". Pass from_citizenship (ISO alpha-2 array) + goal. Privacy: an anonymised record of the query (citizenships, tax residence, goal, budget band and timeline; no name, contact or exact amount) is kept for 90 days to improve coverage.

from_tax_residence.description: ISO alpha-2 tax residence (defaults to first citizenship)

goal.description: What the applicant is optimising for, in plain words: visa-free travel, tax residence, family relocation.

budget_usd.description: Total budget the applicant has available for the investment itself, in USD (fees are additional).

timeline_months.description: Target time to the outcome, in MONTHS.

physical_presence_tolerance.description: How much time the applicant can spend in-country: "none", "minimal", "flexible", "relocating".

tools.name: find_pathways
tools.description: Find which countries offer a given immigration pathway (e.g. digital-nomad, skilled-work, ancestry-descent, retirement-passive, eu-free-movement). Returns the screened countries that have it, each with its key requirements (income thresholds included), cost and path to PR. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens moving within the EU/EEA or Switzerland use eu-free-movement, not a visa.

pathway.description: Pathway id. eu-free-movement = living in another EU/EEA state or Switzerland as an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen.

tools.name: find_retirement_routes
tools.description: Find RETIREMENT and PASSIVE-INCOME residence routes (pensionado, rentista, retiree visas) that qualify on income or savings, not an investment. Filter by monthly income in USD, income type, net worth, the most days a year you want to spend there, region, dependants and untaxed foreign income. golden_only returns only routes rated Golden by the Mirabello Golden Retirement Index (score 70+/100: no investment, little or no tax on foreign income, little presence, little renewal); min_score sets a score floor. Each route gives its official requirement in its legal currency, whether you appear to qualify (indicative FX), the stay rule, the foreign-income tax label (Mexico, Portugal, Colombia and Brazil tax the foreign pension of a tax resident), the Golden Retirement score with its reasons, the path to permanent residence, and the official source. Unverified figures are withheld, never estimated. Information, not advice.

monthly_income_usd.description: Your regular monthly income in USD (pension and/or passive income). Optional; without it qualification by income is left open.

income_type.description: What the income is: pension (state or private retirement pension), passive (rents, dividends, interest), or either/both. Default either.

net_worth_usd.description: Liquid savings or investable net worth in USD, for routes that accept a deposit, savings balance or assets instead of income. Optional.

max_stay_days_per_year.description: The most days a year you are willing to spend in the country. Routes with a higher stated minimum are excluded; routes whose stay rule is not stated are kept and flagged.

foreign_income_untaxed_only.description: true = only routes where foreign income is untaxed for a tax resident (exempt, territorial or remittance basis). Default false.

region.description: Region filter, case-insensitive: e.g. "Latin America", "Caribbean", "Europe", "Asia", "Middle East", "Americas".

detail.description: summary (default for clients on a current MCP version): compact rows with the requirement, stay rule, tax label and Golden Retirement score. full: the complete record of each route.

dependants.description: Number of dependants (spouse, children) to include; routes with a per-dependant income add-on raise the requirement accordingly. Default 0.

golden_only.description: true = only routes rated Golden by the Mirabello Golden Retirement Index; results are then ordered by score. Default false.

min_score.description: Only routes with a Golden Retirement score at or above this value (0 to 100); unscored routes are excluded. Results are then ordered by score.

limit.description: Maximum results returned (default 5, up to 62). The list is ranked; total_matched gives the full count.

tools.name: find_fastest_citizenship
tools.description: Naturalisation periods and NATIONALITY-BASED FAST TRACKS, verified against the enacted statute. Pass nationality (ISO-3166 alpha-2 of the passport held) to rank covered jurisdictions by how soon THAT nationality may apply for citizenship — e.g. an Ibero-American national reaches Spanish citizenship in 2 years instead of 10 (Codigo Civil art. 22.1), a CPLP national reaches Portuguese citizenship in 7 instead of 10 (Lei 37/81 art. 6 as amended by Lei Organica 1/2026). Pass cc instead for one jurisdiction in full, including the ordinary baseline, who gets NO reduction, and any transitional regime. Periods are qualifying residence before an application may be made and exclude processing time. Coverage is narrow by design — a jurisdiction appears only once its statute has been read in full, so absence means unverified, never that no fast track exists. NOT for buying a passport: for citizenship by investment (the fastest second passport for a budget) use the programme listing or recommendation tools.

nationality.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 of the passport held, e.g. BR, AR, WS, NZ

cc.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 of the destination jurisdiction, e.g. ES, PT, NZ, AU

bloc.description: Limit the ranking to one bloc, e.g. EU for "fastest EU passport". One call returns every covered member ranked, with presence and requirements, plus the members not yet covered.

tools.name: get_family_pathway
tools.description: FAMILY PATHWAYS: who can come with, or join, the main applicant — spouse, unmarried/same-sex partner, children (MAXIMUM AGE and when age is measured), adult dependent children, parents, siblings — whether they join at the SAME TIME or LATER, what happens if a child ages out, and every related cost by dependant category. Three modes. (1) programme_id: dependants record of one investment-migration programme, e.g. antigua-cbi, greece-gv. (2) cc: family-reunification law of a country by sponsor class (citizen, resident, investor-visa holder): relatives, waiting period, income and housing tests, fees, processing time. (3) screen: pass children_ages (e.g. [7,15,24]) plus optional parents, partner, together_required to rank programmes that can include the WHOLE family, per person. Each figure carries legal basis, source tier and date. Absence means UNVERIFIED, never that no route exists. Information, not legal advice.

programme_id.description: A programme id from list_programmes, e.g. antigua-cbi

cc.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 of the country whose family-reunification law you need, e.g. PT, AE, US

sponsor.description: Filter the cc routes by sponsor class: citizen, permanent_resident, temporary_resident, investor_visa_holder, worker, student

children_ages.description: Ages of the children (completed years) for screen mode, e.g. [7,15,24]

parents.description: Screen mode: parents must be includable

partner.description: Screen mode: include an unmarried partner who is not a spouse

together_required.description: Screen mode: everyone must be includable in the SAME application (no later add-on)

type.description: Screen mode: limit to citizenship or residence programmes

tools.name: get_emigration_flows
tools.description: OFFICIAL GERMAN EMIGRATION DATA: where German citizens actually move, by destination country and year (Destatis statistic 12711-0008, 2016 onwards). Returns departures, arrivals and net migration per destination, plus each destination share of the NAMED-destination base. Revealed preference, not opinion: in 2025 at least 288,579 German citizens deregistered for a move abroad, a net loss of about 96,689; Switzerland, Austria, Spain, the United States and France were the largest stated destinations. CRITICAL, returned in the caveats field: roughly 48% of departures state NO destination, so rankings describe the named base only, and totals are a floor because people leave without deregistering. Never trend across 2015/2016 (definitional break). Popularity is not suitability. Pass year, destination or top. Licence dl-de/by-2-0; Destatis attribution mandatory on reuse.

year.description: e.g. "2025"; defaults to the latest available

destination.description: destination country name in German, e.g. "Schweiz", or a fragment

tools.name: get_capital_controls
tools.description: CAPITAL MOBILITY — can money legally LEAVE this country, and how much? For an ORIGIN jurisdiction returns the exchange-control regime (free | liberalising | controlled), the annual outbound allowance or remittance scheme (e.g. India LRS USD 250,000/year under FEMA; China SAFE USD 50,000/year), the cash-declaration threshold, the regulator, and what it means for FUNDING an investment-migration programme (whether and how the investment can lawfully be transferred out of the origin country). Pass cc for one jurisdiction; omit for all, or filter by regime. Information, not legal/tax/financial advice — exchange-control rules change frequently; verify with the central bank or local counsel.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 origin country code (e.g. IN, CN, ZA)

tools.name: check_visa_requirement
tools.description: VISA REQUIREMENT for ONE nationality travelling to ONE destination: visa-free (with maximum stay in days where published), visa on arrival, e-visa, electronic travel authorisation, visa required, or no admission. Covers 199 passports x 199 destinations from the open Passport Index dataset, with the Wikipedia corroboration page and the IATA Travel Centre verification link returned alongside. General information only - entry rules change without notice; the destination authority is final.

from_nationality.description: passport held - ISO alpha-2 code or country name, e.g. NG, IN, "Nigeria"

destination.description: destination - ISO alpha-2 code or country name, e.g. TR, "Turkey", "Schengen" (checked via Germany)

tools.name: list_visa_free_destinations
tools.description: ALL destinations for ONE nationality grouped by requirement: visa-free (with maximum stay days where published), visa on arrival, e-visa, electronic travel authorisation, visa required, no admission - plus the counts and a visa-free-plus-on-arrival mobility total. From the open Passport Index dataset (199 passports); general information, verify before travel.

from_nationality.description: passport held - ISO alpha-2 code or country name

tools.name: get_name_change
tools.description: LEGAL NAME CHANGE rules for a jurisdiction: whether a change is permitted, on what grounds (or none), which authority decides (civil registry or court), who may apply, the process, indicative cost and timeline, the effect on the passport, transliteration rules for rendering a name into Latin script, and whether the former name persists on records held abroad. Commonly needed after marriage, after naturalisation, and when a non-Latin name must be rendered consistently across documents. Pass cc for one jurisdiction; omit for the covered list. Decided solely by the competent registry or court; Mirabello informs and orchestrates but does not file applications. Information, not legal advice.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code, e.g. GB, AE, CH

tools.name: get_foundation_rules
tools.description: CHARITABLE & PRIVATE FOUNDATION and TRUST rules for a jurisdiction: whether the foundation legal form exists (Stiftung / fondation / fundación / waqf / foundation company), legal basis, regulator/registry, minimum endowment, governance organs, founder reserved powers, beneficiary rights, charitable-purpose requirements, tax treatment and cross-border donor deductibility, reporting/audit duties, UBO-register visibility, trust recognition (domestic trust law / Hague Convention / not recognised) and lawful foundation+trust combination patterns. Deepens the charity and trust jurisdiction shortlists to 194-country coverage. Pass cc for one jurisdiction; omit for the covered list. Establishment is decided by the competent registry or regulator and executed via licensed local partners; tax outcomes follow the founder's and beneficiaries' residence. Information, not legal or tax advice.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code, e.g. LI, CH, AE

tools.name: get_nonresident_banking
tools.description: Includes basic_account_right: whether residents (or EEA residents) have a statutory right to a basic account; that right is not a ban on non-residents. BANK-ACCOUNT ACCESS for FOREIGN NON-RESIDENTS in a jurisdiction — two profiles: (a) non-resident individual, (b) foreign entity. Each carries the STATUTORY position AND the PRACTICAL bank appetite separately (many countries are legally open but practically closed — the two are never merged), plus typical KYC/document set, remote-opening availability, indicative minimums (bank policy, never law), timelines, CRS/FATCA notes and EDD triggers. Deepens the formation-linked banking landscape to 194-country coverage. Pass cc for one jurisdiction; omit for the covered list. Account opening is decided unilaterally by each bank — NO account opening is ever guaranteed; full CRS/FATCA transparency always. Information, not financial or legal advice.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code, e.g. AE, CH, SG

tools.name: get_property_law
tools.description: REAL-ESTATE LAW FOR FOREIGN BUYERS in a jurisdiction ("can a foreigner buy a house in X?"): whether foreigners may own freehold (unrestricted / restricted zones / leasehold-only / approval required / prohibited), restricted categories (border, agricultural, coastal), approval regimes (e.g. Lex Koller, FIRB), which ownership vehicles a foreigner may lawfully use (direct / local company / foreign company / trust / foundation), purchase taxes and foreign-buyer surcharges, holding taxes on non-resident owners, rental restrictions, repatriation of proceeds, golden-visa linkage and inheritance by foreign heirs. Federal states (US, CH, AU, CA, AE) are flagged subnational: no single country-wide answer is inferred. The law behind a purchase, not listings. Pass cc for one jurisdiction; omit for the covered list. Rules change without notice; conveyancing runs via licensed local professionals. Information, not legal, tax or investment advice.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 country code, e.g. CH, AE, PT

tools.name: get_entry_requirements
tools.description: ENTRY REQUIREMENTS for a DESTINATION: passport-validity rule (the "6-month rule", the Schengen "issued within the previous 10 years AND valid 3 months beyond departure" cap, blank-page requirements) and health/vaccination entry rules (e.g. yellow-fever certificate). Operationally critical: a valid-looking passport is refused BOARDING if it fails these, and the Schengen 10-year issuance cap invalidates passports whose printed expiry is still in the future. Pass cc for one destination; omit for all. Information, not advice — rules and airline enforcement vary by nationality and change without notice.

cc.description: ISO alpha-2 destination country code

tools.name: get_country_tax
tools.description: HNWI tax profile for a country (wealth-protection view): personal income tax (worldwide vs territorial), capital gains, inheritance/estate, wealth tax, exit tax, CRS/AEOI status and special regimes (non-dom, lump-sum, NHR/IFICI, flat-tax). For Switzerland also canton and commune tax at standard household profiles (field subnational), for "which canton taxes least" or "Geneva vs Zug". From official/Tier-A sources. Informational only — not tax advice. ISO alpha-2 code or country name.

tools.name: find_low_tax

Returns matching countries with their HNWI tax + CRS + EU-list (+ crypto) snapshot. Combine with a residence or citizenship route for a full tax-plus-pathway view.

no_inheritance_tax.description: True to require no inheritance or estate tax.

no_wealth_tax.description: True to require no net-wealth tax.

no_capital_gains_tax.description: True to require no capital-gains tax.

tools.name: find_trust_jurisdictions

Tax follows the owner. No structure is recommended. General information, not advice.

tools.description: Filter reference profiles by facts: remote_only, max_setup_usd, banking_tier (good or moderate access), eu_clean (not on EU or FATF lists at the dated snapshot), lane (company or trust). Results are alphabetical, not ranked or recommended. General information, not advice.

tools.description: Side-by-side facts for 2-6 structures by profile key: tax facts, indicative costs, timeline, substance, list status, caveats and who each does not suit. Comparison only, no recommendation. General information, not advice.

Tax follows the owner. It does not recommend a structure and does not plan for the person. Stops for sanctions-affected country links. General information, not advice.

tools.name: get_regulator_registry

Pass cc for one jurisdiction, or international:true for the supranational bodies.

The depth behind headline rates. Use ISO alpha-2. Indicative, not advice.

Use when someone moves and asks what proves they left their old tax residence or started the new one. Tests and factors only — NOT a residence determination. ISO alpha-2 code or country name.

Grounded in FATF/Wolfsberg standards + programme due-diligence rules. INFORMATION ONLY — lists the evidence usually required, never asserts a case is compliant. Call with no args to list available origins and contexts.

States the default legal rules — NOT how any estate will devolve. Use ISO alpha-2.

tools.description: Default matrimonial-property regime for a jurisdiction (e.g. community of acquisitions vs separation of property), whether prenuptial/marital agreements can vary it, and how property splits on divorce or death. Informational — confirm with local counsel. Use ISO alpha-2.

cc.description: Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "PT", "AE", "KN") or its name in any of the 11 site languages ("Portugal", "Schweiz", "UAE"); input_notes shows how it was read.

tools.name: succession_conflict_map
tools.description: Cross-border succession conflict-of-laws position for a jurisdiction: which law governs succession (habitual residence / nationality / situs of assets), EU Succession Regulation 650/2012 (Brussels IV) applicability and whether a professio juris (choice of national law in a will) is available, any clawback of lifetime gifts into reserved shares or renvoi, plus trust/foundation interaction and the headline cross-border planning point. Informational, not advice. Use ISO alpha-2.

cc.description: Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "PT", "AE", "KN") or its name in any of the 11 site languages ("Portugal", "Schweiz", "UAE"); input_notes shows how it was read.

tools.name: choice_of_law_options
tools.description: Which law may govern a cross-border family succession, matrimonial property and divorce, and whether NATIONALITY opens an election. From nationalities held, habitual residence, asset situs and marital status, returns the default applicable law (EU Succession Reg 650/2012 Art 21; Swiss PILA last domicile), the instruments in scope (650/2012 Art 22; Matrimonial Property Reg 2016/1103 Art 22, 18 states; Rome III Art 5, 17 states; Swiss professio juris Arts 90-91), the elections available, hard TIMING rules (2016/1103 and Rome III need the nationality at the time of the agreement; Swiss professio juris is VOID if Swiss nationality is later acquired), situs overrides (e.g. French Code civil art. 913), and the trade-off: a common-law election swaps a FIXED reserved share for a DISCRETIONARY family claim. Returns no-useful-election where nationality opens nothing. Every election needs a properly executed declaration. INFORMATION ONLY, NOT LEGAL OR TAX ADVICE. Pass ISO alpha-2 codes only, never personal data.

habitual_residence.description: ISO alpha-2 of current habitual residence.

The synthesis view over the tax, residence, structure, reporting and succession layers. Pass scenarios as an array of {cc,pathway} or cc as a comma list (e.g. AE,PT,SG). Informational only, not advice; combine with the immigration route and a specific double-tax-treaty corridor for the full picture.

Pass boolean flags (us_person, crs_reportable, crypto_holder, dac6, pep, cbi_applicant, trust_settlor, large_cash_or_sow). STATELESS — pass only non-identifying flags, never personal data. Informational only, not legal/tax advice, not exhaustive.

cbi_applicant.description: True if the client is applying for citizenship by investment.

rbi_applicant.description: True if the client is applying for residence by investment.

trust_settlor.description: True if the client settles or controls a trust or foundation.

large_cash_or_sow.description: True if large cash movements or a complex source-of-wealth story are involved.

tools.name: get_mobility_optionality
tools.description: Strategic mobility optionality for a jurisdiction: the lawful residence/citizenship ROUTES it offers (investment programmes) with minimum physical presence, family inclusion, path to permanence, processing time and regulator — the planning view of mobility, not passport strength. Passport reach (visa-free count) is included as context only. Pass cc for one jurisdiction, omit for all. INFORMATION, NOT ADVICE; combine with the full immigration profile and a Mirabello consultation.

Each block carries provenance (confidence, verified_date, official sources); low-confidence detail is withheld as CHECK-OFFICIAL-SOURCE. Pass cc for one jurisdiction, omit for all. INFORMATION, NOT ADVICE — government status/timelines change frequently; verify the cited source.

Omit weights for an illustrative default composite. Pass cc for one jurisdiction, or limit for the top N. Pure projection over Mirabello-verified data; illustrative comparative score, NOT advice.

tools.name: search_properties
tools.description: Search Mirabello-advised investment real estate that QUALIFIES for a citizenship- or residency-by-investment programme. Filter by country, programme (e.g. "grenada-citizenship-by-investment", "greece-golden-visa"), type (CBI|RBI), budget_max (USD, FX-normalised best-effort), beds_min, listing_type (villa|apartment|residence|plot), sale_status. Returns priced listings with the qualifying programme, availability, and the Mirabello enquiry route. Mirabello Consultancy acts as introducer only (it does not sell or broker property); there is no direct developer contact, and all buyer enquiries are routed through Mirabello. Indicative figures; book a consultation to confirm.

Each call sends a separate enquiry, so do not repeat a call that succeeded.
